subject: Trading
title: The Right, Not the Obligation
description: A 60-second lesson on The Right, Not the Obligation.

hook.text: An option gives you the right to buy or sell a stock at a specific price—but you never have to. That's the magic.

buildup.text: Unlike buying stock, where you own the asset, an option is a contract that grants a choice for a limited time.

discovery.text: You pay a premium—the price of the option—for this right. If the trade works, you exercise. If not, you walk away.

twist.text: Your maximum loss with a long option is the premium you paid. But the potential gain can be many times larger.

climax.text: Options create asymmetry: limited risk with unlimited upside. That's why they appeal to traders worldwide.

punchline.text: Pay a small fee for a big opportunity.

quiz.question: What does buying an option give you?
options: An obligation to buy or sell
The right, but not obligation, to buy or sell at a specific price
